task.description:
Design artefact for REQ-037 (Promotion review state machine and base promote -- promotion_review.zig PRM-04 + promotion.zig ENV-03). Read REQ-037's full entry in docs/requirements.yaml (search 'id: REQ-037') -- it names the exact functions, gates, and the 7 permitted state edges in detail. Also read lib/letflow/definitions/promotion_review.ex in full (REQ-035's existing Ecto schema -- confirm exact field names: tenant_id, plan_digest, def_type, def_id, serialised_plan, status, requested_by, approved_by, approved_at, superseded_by, row_version), lib/letflow/definitions/promotion_plan.ex and promotion_digest.ex (REQ-036's PromotionPlan.t()/plan_entry() and verify_digest/2 -- insert_review/1 consumes REQ-036's plan+digest, approve_review/4's digest-mismatch check calls verify_digest/2), docs/guides/backend_developer_guide.md, and REQ-036's own design doc lib/letflow/design/promotion_plan.md sec 9.1 (the permission-check gap that recurs here per REQ-037's own moduledoc note -- do not silently invent a different resolution than REQ-036's opts[:permission_checker] pattern without justification; consistency across sibling requirements matters).

Produce lib/letflow/design/promotion_review_state_machine.md covering:
1. State machine: exactly 7 permitted edges (pending_review->approved, pending_review->rejected, approved->applied, approved->failed, applied->superseded, failed->superseded, rejected->superseded [the NEW edge]). Every other transition must return the same invalid-transition error regardless of which illegal edge was attempted -- state this as an explicit design invariant, not left implicit.
2. insert_review/1(plan, digest, requested_by) -> {:ok, review} | {:error, :duplicate_review} -- consumes REQ-036's PromotionPlan.t()/digest, row_version: 1, tenant_id/def_id/def_type from the plan. Map REQ-035's partial unique index violation to the distinct duplicate-review error (not a generic Ecto.ConstraintError leak).
3. approve_review/4(review_id, actor_id, plan_digest, opts) -- full @spec, gates IN ORDER: (a) reviewer != requested_by (self-approval forbidden) BEFORE any row update, (b) status == pending_review, (c) plan_digest matches stored value exactly (call PromotionDigest.verify_digest/2), (d) UPDATE ... WHERE row_version = $expected -- zero rows affected -> invalid-transition error, not a silent no-op. State the exact error atom for each distinct gate failure (self-approval error distinct from digest-mismatch distinct from invalid-transition).
4. reject_review/2(review_id, actor_id) -- pending_review -> rejected, no digest check, no self-rejection restriction (explicit per prm-05).
5. mark_review_applied/1, mark_review_failed/1 -- approved -> applied / approved -> failed, driven by REQ-040 (not built yet, not this requirement's concern -- just the transition functions).
6. supersede_review/2(review_id, superseded_by_event_id) -- applied|failed|rejected -> superseded, all 3 edges via the same function (not 3 separate functions) unless there's a good reason to split.
7. promote_definition/N (Letflow.Definitions.Promotion or similar new module) -- the version-pointer-move + event-append operation mark_review_applied's caller invokes; reuse REQ-036's permission-check-shape pattern (opts[:permission_checker]) and tenant-type-check pattern (opts[:tenant_classifier]) rather than inventing new ones -- state explicitly if REQ-037 needs different opts or can share REQ-036's exact shape.

For each of the 6 acceptance criteria, map to a concrete design element. Concurrency handling for approve_review/4's row_version optimistic lock must be spelled out precisely (this is testable via 2 concurrent calls per AC4 -- the design must make clear how a test can deterministically produce this race, e.g. by manually racing two Repo.update_all calls or by testing the WHERE-clause semantics directly without needing real concurrency). No implementation code -- signatures/types/algorithm prose only.
acceptance_criteria: Every one of REQ-037's 6 acceptance criteria maps to a concrete design element in lib/letflow/design/promotion_review_state_machine.md
All 7 permitted edges enumerated explicitly with their guard conditions; the invalid-transition catch-all for every non-edge stated as an explicit invariant
approve_review/4's 3 gates (self-approval, status, digest) sequenced explicitly with distinct error atoms per failure, plus the row_version optimistic-lock mechanism
insert_review/1's duplicate-review error mapped explicitly from REQ-035's partial unique index constraint violation
promote_definition/N's relationship to REQ-036's permission_checker/tenant_classifier opts pattern addressed explicitly (reuse or explicit divergence with reason)
A concrete, testable mechanism for AC4's 'two concurrent approve_review/4 calls' is spelled out (not left to TEST-DESIGNER to invent)
No implementation code present -- signatures and type shapes only
